usage.result_excerpt:
`main.rs` is written and compiles. I ran Example 2 and got the expected `10`, `10100001111` and `0`. I did not run Example 1 (`255 10 16`) or any large-value cases.

It reads each line as `value from to`, converts the value to a number, then prints it in the target base in upper case. Zero prints as `0`. It uses 128-bit integers, so values up to 2^63 - 1 can't overflow.
